correctness.rationale: For distinct rank-one nonzero Boolean idempotents equality of two nonzero cross-rectangle products forces equality of both original rectangles; hence commuting means both cross-products vanish. The exhaustive classification of coordinate membership patterns has \(2^{k+1}+k-1\) choices, with the k double-singleton requirements enforced by inclusion-exclusion and maximality removing exactly the empty pattern. This proves C(n,k), M(n,k) for all n>=2 and 1<=k<=n. Degree and diameter follow from cross-annihilation. Exhaustive literal-product checks were completed for n<=4, clique/facet/degree/distance checks for n<=5; computations do not prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The selected canonical minimal nonzero Boolean factor-rank stratum has a natural orthogonality/partial-decomposition interpretation. The theorem determines the entire clique complex facet f-vector, every vertex degree, isolates and component diameter uniformly in dimension, including a strong nonpurity phenomenon (maximal cliques of every size 1..n). These invariants cannot be read from the already-known count of idempotent vertices or from full-matrix commuting-graph diameter results.
